evidence.quote: While inflation has come down substantially since last summer, it is still too high, and by some measures progress has been slowing.
inflation in nonhousing services, the largest component of services, has been stubbornly high at around 4.5 percent and shows no signs of significant decline yet.
the current labor market is one of the strongest that U.S. workers have experienced in decades.
I acknowledge that there are downside risks, among them the possibility that the degree of bank lending restraint and uncertainty could weigh on economic activity more than I expect.
History shows that monetary policy works with long and variable lags, and that a year is not a long enough period for demand to feel the full effect of higher interest rates.
I intend to consider all these factors in the coming weeks as I contemplate the appropriate stance of monetary policy going forward.

parsed.rationale: The speech balances still-too-high core inflation and a strong labor market against slowing GDP, lagged effects of policy, and credit-tightening downside risks. It gives no signal of further hikes, which leaves a balanced-to-slightly-dovish lean toward a pause.

spans.quote: While inflation has come down substantially since last summer, it is still too high, and by some measures progress has been slowing.
inflation in nonhousing services, the largest component of services, has been stubbornly high at around 4.5 percent and shows no signs of significant decline yet.
the current labor market is one of the strongest that U.S. workers have experienced in decades.
I acknowledge that there are downside risks, among them the possibility that the degree of bank lending restraint and uncertainty could weigh on economic activity more than I expect.
History shows that monetary policy works with long and variable lags, and that a year is not a long enough period for demand to feel the full effect of higher interest rates.
I intend to consider all these factors in the coming weeks as I contemplate the appropriate stance of monetary policy going forward.
